items.title: China's central bank promises policy support, stronger countercyclical adjustments
items.text: The PBOC is shifting its primary short-term operational target from the seven-day repo rate (DR007) to the overnight rate (DR001), with overnight transactions now comprising over 90% of money market repo trading. Despite global tightening trends, the PBOC plans to introduce incremental policy measures to maintain ample liquidity and low financing costs, signaling a divergence from the hawkish stances of the Fed, ECB, and BOJ.

items.title: Imported Inflation Hits as PBOC Flags Overseas Rate Hikes: This Cycle's Impact Seen as Relatively Mild
items.text: The PBOC identifies Middle East geopolitical tensions and the AI-driven demand boom in semiconductors and power as primary drivers of current global supply-side inflationary pressures. While acknowledging global rate hikes, the PBOC expects this cycle of monetary adjustment to be relatively mild, projecting smaller shocks to global financial markets compared to previous tightening episodes.

items.title: UAE central bank’s seat at the dollar table
items.text: The UAE's monetary policy remains structurally tethered to the US dollar, necessitating close alignment with Federal Reserve interest rate decisions to maintain currency stability. This peg forces the UAE central bank to import US monetary conditions, limiting domestic policy autonomy during periods of global economic divergence or localized inflationary shocks.

items.title: We're encouraged by Wednesday's benign inflation data and strong neocloud earnings
items.text: The July CPI report showed benign inflation, reducing market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve rate hike to 40% and supporting a rally in equities via lower bond yields. Infrastructure-focused cloud providers Coreweave and Nebius saw shares surge 19% and 27% respectively, signaling that massive demand for AI-driven cloud computing remains a primary driver for market performance.

items.title: Small investors became a major stock market force. Now, they risk getting pushed back into the dark
items.text: The SEC is considering a proposal to shift public companies from quarterly to biannual earnings reporting, a move that could create an information vacuum and disadvantage retail investors who rely on frequent disclosures. Market experts warn that reduced transparency could lead to increased misinformation and cause retail participants to become more hesitant toward investing in high-growth, small-cap companies.

items.title: SK Hynix halts bond buying, shifts cash to bank deposits in blow to S.Korean credit market - KED Global
items.text: SK Hynix has abruptly ceased its bond-buying activities, opting instead to move significant cash reserves into commercial bank deposits to prioritize liquidity and potential shareholder returns. This shift by a major corporate issuer creates immediate volatility in the South Korean short-term credit market, potentially forcing other firms to reassess their own liquidity and debt management strategies.

items.title: The $30 trillion Treasury market is facing a painful reckoning. How rising yields could squeeze your portfolio. - MarketWatch
items.text: The $30 trillion U.S. Treasury market is experiencing structural pressure as rising yields threaten to erode the value of existing fixed-income portfolios across the financial sector. Investors must prepare for potential capital losses and increased volatility as the current interest rate environment forces a painful repricing of risk-free assets within institutional and retail portfolios.

items.title: PBOC Q2 Monetary Policy Report: H1 GDP Grows 4.7%, Yuan Strengthens 3% vs Dollar, Creates 1 Trillion Yuan Private Enterprise Relending Facility
items.text: The PBOC has launched a 1 trillion yuan ($149 billion) relending facility specifically for private enterprises, signaling a targeted effort to bolster the private sector amid broader economic structural shifts. Monetary policy is becoming more precise, evidenced by the narrowing of the repo operation corridor to 50 basis points and a 0.25 percentage point rate cut on structural policy tools to lower corporate financing costs.

items.title: Excess savings are driving the new ‘China shock’
items.text: The current 'China shock' is fundamentally different from the past, driven by domestic technological upgrading rather than low-cost labor mobilization, which is creating significant global manufacturing capacity shifts. Weak domestic demand is forcing Chinese firms to export excess production, potentially leading to increased trade tensions as global markets absorb the surge in Chinese manufactured goods.

items.title: Hong Kong property recovery faces new risk as Beijing widens offshore tax net
items.text: Beijing's implementation of a 20% personal income tax on offshore investment returns threatens to dampen mainland demand for Hong Kong real estate and insurance products. UBS analysts estimate this tax could compress net rental yields on residential properties from 2.2% to 1.8%, potentially eroding the asset class's attractiveness to mainland investors.

items.title: HK wins back foreign professionals as financial sector rebounds
items.text: Recruitment data indicates a reversal of the pandemic-era talent drain to Singapore, with seven out of ten fund companies now prioritizing Hong Kong for their Asian base. The resurgence in IPO fundraising and strong performance of the Hang Seng Index are driving renewed demand for office space and professional services, signaling a stabilization in the financial sector.

items.title: Forget chatbot training. AI's next big data grab is about learning how humans work.
items.text: Tech giants are shifting development strategies from static text-based training to 'reinforcement learning environments,' where AI agents simulate real-world workplace tasks like coding and software navigation to improve autonomous performance. Major firms are aggressively securing proprietary behavioral data, with Google reportedly in talks to invest $1.5 billion in startup Mechanize, while Meta and SpaceX are actively collecting internal employee activity data to train next-generation agents.

items.title: From Apple to Netflix: Why Big Tech is pushing deeper into gaming ecosystem
items.text: Big Tech companies are integrating gaming deeper into their hardware and service stacks to increase consumer 'stickiness' and justify high-end silicon upgrades, such as Apple's implementation of hardware-accelerated ray tracing. The strategy focuses on cross-platform ecosystem continuity, allowing users to maintain progress across devices, which serves as a defensive moat to retain users within proprietary hardware and subscription environments.

items.title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
items.text: Economic data from the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research indicates that unemployment rates for workers most exposed to AI have risen by only 0.77 percentage points since 2022, trailing the 0.85 percentage-point increase seen in less-exposed sectors. The lack of mass displacement suggests that AI is currently functioning as a tool for labor augmentation rather than replacement, mirroring the slow, multi-decade integration timeline observed during the historical computer revolution.

items.title: Can AI fight AI? Where the security gap still exists in cybersecurity, and how MSPs can help.
items.text: A 2026 Proofpoint report reveals that 50% of organizations utilizing AI-based security controls still suffered from confirmed or suspicious AI-related incidents, highlighting a significant gap between rapid AI adoption and security maturity. While 87% of firms have moved AI assistants beyond pilot stages, over half lack confidence in their ability to detect compromised AI agents, creating a lucrative market opportunity for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) to bridge the operational security deficit.

items.title: Nvidia and Wall Street partners launch $500 billion AI infrastructure financing platform
items.text: Nvidia has partnered with major financial institutions including BlackRock, Blackstone, and Goldman Sachs to create a $500 billion vehicle designed to finance data centers and GPU clusters for customers. This initiative shifts AI compute from a capital-intensive purchase to a financed infrastructure asset, aiming to sustain Nvidia's revenue growth while keeping credit risk off its own balance sheet.

items.title: Meta and Nvidia expand open-weight AI model offerings to compete with proprietary systems
items.text: Nvidia released its Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model, providing developers with full access to training datasets and model weights to compete against closed-source models from OpenAI and Anthropic. The move aligns with a broader industry push to prevent premature regulatory restrictions on open-weight AI, which proponents argue will foster competition and maintain American technological leadership.

items.title: Nvidia found a new way to keep the AI boom funded: your retirement money
items.text: Nvidia is partnering with major financial institutions like BlackRock and KKR to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure, effectively shifting the burden of capital expenditure from Big Tech balance sheets to institutional investors. By structuring AI compute as a long-term infrastructure asset similar to toll roads, these vehicles aim to securitize future cash flows from AI usage, allowing pension and insurance capital to fund the massive hardware requirements of the AI boom.

items.title: Dominion ordered to directly assign some transmission costs to data centers
items.text: The Virginia State Corporation Commission has mandated that Dominion Energy directly assign transmission infrastructure costs to data centers, moving away from broad-based rate recovery that previously impacted residential customers. This regulatory shift forces data center operators to internalize the costs of grid expansion, potentially altering the economics of site selection and increasing the capital intensity of new developments in high-demand regions.

items.title: SpaceX could make $500 billion in 2028, Elon Musk says
items.text: Elon Musk has projected that SpaceX could generate $500 billion in annual revenue by 2028, signaling an aggressive scaling of its satellite and launch operations. This valuation target implies a massive expansion beyond current launch services, likely driven by the deployment of 100,000 Starlink V3 satellites and a potential fleet of one million AI-focused data center satellites.

items.title: Firefly Aerospace pushes debut of Alpha Block 2 rocket to the fourth quarter of 2026
items.text: Firefly Aerospace reported a $25.8 million increase in R&D costs for Q2 2026, primarily attributed to production scaling for its Alpha Block 2 configuration and associated engineering upgrades. Despite the launch delay to Q4 2026, the company has secured the majority of its 2027 launch manifest and expanded its hypersonic task orders, indicating strong commercial and government demand.

items.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
items.text: Enterprise AI agents currently have access to only 45% of organizational data on average, creating a significant bottleneck for autonomous decision-making. Gartner projects that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, necessitating a shift away from restrictive legacy data architectures. Data leaders who provide agents with access to over 70% of enterprise information report higher ROI and greater success compared to laggards who provide access to 30% or less. Effective agentic AI requires frictionless, real-time integration across structured and unstructured data sources, including supply chain and HR systems, to ensure trustworthy outcomes.

items.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
items.text: - The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year. - BYD will have a dedicated group pavilion in Hall 9, with Huawei's HIMA, Xpeng and Nio also attending. The 29th Chengdu International Automobile Exhibition (2026 Chengdu Auto Show) will be held from August 21 to 30 at the Western China Expo City in Chengdu, Sichuan province, making it China's first A-level auto show... The show will cover 220,000 square meters and bring together nearly 120 domestic and international brands as well as about 1,600 display vehicles, the organizer said on Wednesday. As one of China's five A-level auto shows, the Chengdu event is seen as a barometer of demand in the southwestern Chinese market.

items.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
items.text: - The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September. - The mid-size electric sedan was developed under the lead of Hyundai's China design center, tailored for Chinese users and planned for export to global markets. Hyundai's electric comeback in China is about to deliver its first result. Beijing Hyundai's Ioniq V will open pre-sales on August 21 at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show and go on sale officially in September. That timeline comes from reports by several Chinese auto media, with the September launch previously disclosed by Beijing Hyundai general manager Li Fenggang.

items.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
items.text: - Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units. - The key variable for the second half is the new Sky Nomad product line. Xiaomi EV, the electric vehicle unit of Xiaomi (HKEX: 1810), delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, up 2.68% year-on-year but down 9.99% from june, according to data released Tuesday by the China Passenger Car... This marked Xiaomi EV's fourth consecutive month with deliveries above 30,000 units, although year-on-year growth was nearly flat. The company delivered 30,452 vehicles in July last year.

items.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
items.text: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure. Transitioning to linear optics eliminates the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, potentially reducing module power consumption by up to 50%. The new PHY IP addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks in dense AI racks, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G connectivity and co-packaged optics (CPO). Measured performance data indicates that the IP meets or exceeds OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for TX VMA, jitter, and RX JTOL, ensuring interoperability in high-speed data center environments.

items.title: mikehasa/agentacct
items.text: Tech Stack: Python-based local-first architecture designed to intercept and parse agent logs. Purpose: Provides granular visibility into agentic workflows, including token consumption, latency, and tool execution success. Use Cases: Financial auditing of AI development costs, debugging agentic task failures, and optimizing prompt engineering for cost-efficiency. Compatibility: Supports popular coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenDevin. A local-first observability and cost-tracking dashboard specifically designed for AI coding agents.

items.title: simonlin1212/vibe-astock
items.text: Tech Stack: Python-based dashboard that separates deterministic financial calculations from AI-driven narrative synthesis. Purpose: Visualizes market sentiment, liquidity flow, and 'money-making' effects without relying on LLM hallucinations for core data. Use Cases: Real-time monitoring of A-share limit-up pools, ladder tiers, and institutional capital flows for short-term traders. Privacy: Operates entirely locally, allowing users to integrate LLMs for analysis without exposing sensitive trading data via API keys. A local-first A-share market sentiment and short-term trading dashboard using deterministic metrics.

items.title: Flaminis/Dalaran
items.text: Tech Stack: Rust-based architecture, hard-forked from Rerun, optimized for high-throughput robotics and sensor data. Purpose: Provides a robust framework for visualizing and analyzing complex, time-synchronized multimodal datasets. Use Cases: Analyzing high-frequency financial time-series data, sensor fusion in robotics, and debugging complex event-driven systems. Compatibility: Native support for existing .rrd recordings and seamless integration with ROS 2 ecosystems. A high-performance, ROS 2-native visualization and data infrastructure for multimodal time-series analysis.

items.title: US yield curve twists expose Trump's and Bessent's rate dilemma - Reuters
items.text: Recent volatility in the US yield curve is creating a complex policy environment for political and economic leadership, specifically regarding interest rate management. The shifting curve dynamics complicate the outlook for fiscal and monetary coordination. Investors are closely monitoring how these yield curve twists reflect broader concerns about future inflation and growth, which directly influence the sustainability of current Treasury market valuations.

items.title: China's NEV sales rise 23.7% in July, with exports surging 1.5 times, CAAM data shows
items.text: Total NEV sales reached 1.56 million units in July, with exports surging 150% year-over-year to 553,000 units, effectively offsetting the weakness in domestic consumer demand. The data reveals a critical divergence where export growth is becoming the primary engine for Chinese manufacturers, pushing total vehicle exports above 1 million units for the second consecutive month.

items.title: Exclusive | Bank of America to Deploy $250 Billion to Bolster AI and Energy Infrastructure
items.text: Bank of America has committed $250 billion toward U.S. infrastructure, with a specific strategic focus on financing the massive capital requirements for AI-driven data centers and energy grid upgrades. This capital deployment signals a major institutional bet on the long-term viability of AI infrastructure, likely lowering the cost of capital for hyperscalers and energy developers in the sector.

items.text: AMD reported 34.3% revenue growth in fiscal year 2025 to $34.6 billion, bolstered by strategic partnerships with OpenAI and the integration of ZT Design to capture data center demand. While AMD maintains a strong balance sheet with a 0.1x debt-to-equity ratio, investors must weigh its high stock-based compensation, which accounted for 21.2% of operating cash flow in 2025.

items.title: VinSpace Announces Launch Contract with SpaceX, Marking a New Milestone for Vietnam's Space Industry
items.text: Vietnam-based VinSpace has contracted with SpaceX for a 2027 rideshare mission, signaling the emergence of new international commercial space participants utilizing established launch infrastructure. The contract supports VinSpace's vertical integration strategy, as the company aims to develop end-to-end capabilities ranging from satellite design and manufacturing to on-orbit operations and data services.

items.title: Iran to join BRICS development bank soon, central bank governor says
items.text: Iran is set to join the BRICS New Development Bank (NDB), a strategic move intended to bypass U.S. sanctions and establish alternative financial channels outside the dollar-denominated system. The move aligns with broader BRICS efforts to promote trade in national currencies, potentially fragmenting global financial infrastructure and reducing the efficacy of Western-led economic sanctions.

items.title: Gold is glittering again – but that’s not necessarily good news
items.text: Gold prices have surged over 8% in the past week to trade above $4,400 per ounce, driven by market concerns regarding U.S. fiscal integrity and a potential shift in Federal Reserve priorities toward growth over inflation control. The metal's recent rally reflects a 'debasement trade' and a flight to safety, signaling that investors are increasingly hedging against the risk of stagflation and potential political interference in U.S. monetary policy.

items.title: How much time does AI save at work? New Census Bureau data breaks it down.
items.text: Approximately 55% of workers now utilize AI, with 30% of users reporting time savings of one to two hours per task, though 15% report even higher efficiency gains of three to four hours. The data highlights a 'J-curve' productivity trend where initial adoption often causes temporary dips in output due to learning friction, suggesting that immediate ROI may be lower than long-term expectations.

items.text: While Q2 2026 profit growth exceeded 30%, Bank of America strategists warn that earnings growth is expected to decelerate below 20% by Q1 2027, a transition historically associated with lower market returns. Corporate America is currently delivering the steepest earnings-estimate revision path in at least 26 years, with 85.2% of companies beating EPS expectations, the highest rate since 2021.

items.title: Tesla And BYD Are Reframing An Age Old Stock Market Question
items.text: Tesla reported a 25.5% revenue increase to $28.24B, yet operating margins compressed to 1.4% and free cash flow turned negative at $1.09B due to heavy AI-related capital expenditures. The divergence between Tesla's high-multiple software-centric valuation and BYD's focus on vertical integration and hardware volume highlights a fundamental debate regarding the sustainability of AI-driven growth versus traditional manufacturing durability.

items.title: Nvidia's $70 billion bet on OpenAI, Anthropic, and others could pay off big for shareholders
items.text: Nvidia has committed $70 billion in equity investments into key ecosystem partners, including $30 billion in OpenAI and $10 billion in Anthropic, positioning the company to capture value from future IPOs. Analysts view these investments as highly manageable, representing only 15% of the $470 billion in free cash flow Nvidia is projected to generate through 2027, supporting its ongoing capital return program.

items.title: Tesla Retail Sales In China Drop 32%, Even As The Battery EV Market Gains
items.text: Tesla's retail sales in China experienced a sharp 32% decline in July, significantly underperforming the broader battery electric vehicle market and highlighting potential market share erosion. Despite the sales slump, the Model Y remains a top-tier performer in China, ranking second in popularity behind Geely’s lower-priced Xingyuan hatchback, indicating a shift in consumer preference toward budget-friendly domestic alternatives.

items.title: Strong AI earnings lift S&P 500, Nasdaq as inflation data calms rate-hike jitters
items.text: Market sentiment received a dual boost from benign inflation data, which reduced investor anxiety regarding potential interest rate hikes, and robust earnings reports from the AI infrastructure sector. The broad-based rally in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reflects a shift in investor focus toward companies demonstrating tangible demand for AI-related hardware and cloud computing services.

items.title: AI infrastructure stocks surge after strong earnings from CoreWeave, Supermicro
items.text: The 'picks and shovels' trade is intensifying as companies like Supermicro and CoreWeave report blowout results, signaling that demand for AI server racks and liquid cooling technology is accelerating. With 87% of S&P 500 companies reporting earnings so far beating estimates by a median of 7%, the infrastructure sector is proving to be a critical beneficiary of sustained corporate AI investment.

items.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
items.text: Imec researchers evaluated 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFET architectures for the A2 node, utilizing a 36 nm contacted poly pitch (CPP) and 10 nm gate length. The study concludes that 2D GAA CFETs do not currently offer a scaling advantage over silicon GAA CFETs at the A2 node due to similar contact formation constraints. Successful implementation of these architectures requires rigorous co-optimization of contact resistance and parasitic extraction to realize potential PPA benefits. The findings highlight the necessity of multiscale power-performance-area (PPA) evaluation frameworks to bridge the gap between theoretical channel advantages and practical fab integration.

items.title: Defect Prediction in Optical Lithography, EUVL, and NIL (National Taiwan University)
items.text: National Taiwan University researchers reviewed the evolution of defect prediction, noting that modern patterning technologies like EUVL and Nanoimprint Lithography (NIL) require new modeling paradigms beyond traditional optical correction. EUVL introduces unique stochastic challenges such as photon-limited variability and mask 3D effects, while NIL shifts defect origins toward viscoelastic deformation and template interaction. The paper advocates for hybrid frameworks that combine physics-based interpretability with data-driven machine learning to improve pattern recognition and uncertainty-aware screening. This shift toward physically grounded, data-efficient prediction is critical for maintaining yield as advanced patterning moves away from simple geometry-driven correction logic.

items.title: Oracle plans more layoffs weeks after spending most of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget
items.text: Oracle is initiating a new round of layoffs to reduce payroll before the second fiscal quarter, following a year where it already eliminated 21,000 positions, or 13% of its total workforce. With $1.8 billion of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget already exhausted, these additional cuts suggest the company may face further financial strain or require a new restructuring plan to manage rising interest expenses and heavy AI-related capex.

items.title: CoreWeave Reports Massive Growth and Long-Term GPU Demand
items.text: CoreWeave reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2.575 billion, a 112% year-over-year increase, and secured an additional $25 billion in contracts in just five weeks following the quarter's end. The company is successfully contracting 2020-vintage Nvidia GPUs through 2029 at full pricing, challenging the bear case regarding hardware obsolescence and proving sustained demand for older silicon.

items.title: Scientists just created female clones of male mice
items.text: Researchers in Japan have successfully used a CRISPR-based technique to remove the Y chromosome from male mouse embryos, effectively creating female clones from male cells. While currently in the preprint stage, this breakthrough challenges the biological assumption that both male and female gametes are strictly required for mammalian reproduction. The technology holds significant potential for wildlife conservation, offering a pathway to rescue endangered species by managing sex ratios or preserving genetic diversity when only male individuals remain. This development builds on previous observations of sex-reversal in nature, such as the Okinawa rubble goby, and could eventually refine current, inefficient cloning methods used for species like black-footed ferrets.

items.title: Nvidia’s $500 billion financing deal for AI infrastructure
items.text: Nvidia is partnering with major financial institutions to create a $500 billion pipeline for financing data centers and GPU clusters, targeting customers who lack the capital or credit to purchase hardware directly. The model faces significant risks, including potential asset depreciation and the threat of a price war from Chinese competitors, which could undermine the long-term value of the financed silicon.

items.title: US EV prices are going back up as discounts shrink
items.text: Average transaction prices for US EVs rose 1.2% in July to $56,126, marking the first annual increase since December as automakers significantly reduced consumer incentives by 24.3% year-over-year. Tesla's average transaction price climbed to $53,891, while the company simultaneously slashed its incentive spending by nearly 34% compared to the previous year, indicating a shift toward margin preservation.

items.title: Nvidia’s $500 billion financing deal threatens custom chips
items.text: Nvidia is partnering with major financial firms to create a $500 billion pipeline for funding data centers and GPU clusters, targeting customers who lack the credit or cash to purchase hardware directly. The strategy faces significant risks, including potential asset depreciation and the threat of a price war from Chinese competitors who are rapidly scaling domestic compute capacity to flood the market with cheaper alternatives.

items.title: Cisco's stock drops despite earnings, revenue beat
items.text: Cisco reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $1.22 per share on $17.25 billion in revenue, both exceeding analyst estimates of $1.17 and $16.82 billion respectively. Despite strong guidance—including a projected revenue increase from hyperscalers to $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027—shares fell as investors reacted to the stock's 60% year-to-date run-up.

items.title: Cerebras stock plunges 14% after second earnings report following IPO
items.text: Cerebras missed second-quarter core revenue expectations, reporting $180 million against a $194 million consensus, despite raising its full-year core revenue outlook to $880-$890 million. The company reported a significant net loss of $450.5 million, largely driven by $386.6 million in stock-compensation costs, even as management emphasized strong demand for its 'fast inference' AI chips.

items.title: Trump Says He Has Told Big Tech Companies to Build Their Own Power Plants
items.text: The administration is pressuring major technology firms to self-fund power generation for data centers, citing the inability of the aging national grid to handle the massive electricity demands of AI infrastructure. This policy shift, intended to shield consumers from rising utility costs, could significantly alter the capital expenditure profiles and long-term operational strategies for hyperscalers like Microsoft and Google.

items.title: Cerebras shares plummet 16% after results fail to impress investors
items.text: Cerebras Systems experienced a significant 16% decline in share price following an earnings report that failed to meet heightened investor expectations for the AI hardware challenger. The market reaction underscores growing investor sensitivity to valuation premiums for AI-focused hardware firms, as participants demand clear evidence of sustained revenue growth and competitive differentiation against established incumbents.

items.title: EVs Excluded From South Korea's Version of IRA, Raising Concerns Across Battery Industry
items.text: The South Korean government's exclusion of electric vehicles from its new Domestic Production Tax Credit program threatens the competitiveness of domestic automakers like Hyundai and Kia against rising Chinese imports. Industry analysts warn of a potential cascading negative impact on the domestic battery supply chain, as lower EV sales volumes for local manufacturers could reduce demand for locally produced battery components.

items.title: AI Infrastructure Boom Drives Industrial Leasing Demand Beyond Data Centers, Cushman & Wakefield Finds
items.text: Data center-related industrial leasing reached 13.5 million square feet in 2025, a 44% increase from 2024, as the AI ecosystem creates massive secondary demand for manufacturers of electrical, cooling, and power infrastructure. The broader economic impact is substantial, with the data center supply chain supporting an estimated 81,000 to 124,000 jobs and generating $11.6 billion in annual gross economic output across major U.S. markets.

items.title: Self-Supervised Layout Generation To Fix Advanced-Node DRVs (Nvidia, Duke)
items.text: Researchers from NVIDIA and Duke University developed SCALE, a self-supervised framework designed to automate the fixing of design-rule violations (DRVs) at sub-2nm nodes. The framework utilizes a domain-adapted Vision-Language Model (VLM) that learns to reconstruct masked layout polygons, providing geometric guidance for complex routing issues. SCALE improves the solve rates of existing automated agents by 12% to 25%, achieving up to 97% success on real-world sub-2nm layout cases. By automating the repair of spacing, width, and color-spacing violations, this technology addresses the growing bottleneck of manual layout fixing in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: Global markets welcome moderate US inflation but Mideast uncertainties limit optimism
items.text: US annual inflation cooled to 3.4% with core inflation hitting a multi-month low of 2.5%, significantly reducing market expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes this year. Geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and uncertainty regarding the extension of the US-Iran ceasefire continue to act as a ceiling on market optimism despite positive domestic economic data.

items.title: Forging Indonesia’s Gold Chain: From Underground Reserves to Central Bank Vaults
items.text: Indonesia holds 3,600 metric tons of gold reserves but maintains only 87.1 tons in official central bank holdings, highlighting a significant strategic mismatch compared to regional peers. Experts are advocating for Bank Indonesia to pivot from holding $145.6 billion in fiat-heavy foreign exchange reserves toward domestic gold accumulation to hedge against global dedollarization.

items.title: AI driving rise in tech stock
items.text: Strong demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving significant equity gains, evidenced by CoreWeave doubling its quarterly revenue and Supermicro exceeding financial expectations. The continued outperformance of AI-related tech firms like Nvidia and Oracle suggests that sector-specific growth remains a primary driver for investors despite broader macroeconomic volatility.

items.text: July consumer price data showed a cooling in annual growth, prompting traders to scale back expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in September. items.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
items.text: Data center operators are preparing for 1-megawatt racks to support the massive power and cooling demands of next-generation AI compute clusters. Hyperscalers including Google, Meta, and Microsoft are collaborating via the OCP 'Mount Diablo' project to standardize rack infrastructure, cooling, and power delivery. The shift necessitates moving away from passive rack enclosures toward integrated compute systems that tightly couple liquid cooling, power shelves, and high-speed interconnects.

items.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
items.text: Copper interconnects are reaching physical limits regarding signal loss and power consumption, forcing a transition to optical interconnects even within rack-scale environments. The industry is redefining scaling terminology to include 'scale-in,' which refers to the bandwidth capacity managed within a single chassis. Optical circuit switching (OCS) is gaining traction as a way to reduce latency and improve GPU utilization, which currently suffers when processors wait for data.

items.title: What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale?
items.text: Co-packaged optics (CPO) is moving from proof-of-concept to production, initially targeting scale-out switch ASICs where copper bandwidth is insufficient. The transition to using CPO in scale-up networks—connecting thousands of XPUs—remains the next major technical hurdle for the industry. Widespread adoption depends on standardizing manufacturing, testing, and supply chain operations to ensure cost-effective, high-volume deployment.

items.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash

The company is scaling an automatic auditing system to flag suspicious search patterns, though it has not yet allowed independent verification of the tool's efficacy. items.text: Experts estimate a 50-50 probability that quantum computers will be capable of breaking 2048-bit RSA encryption by 2040, necessitating a long-term strategic shift in cybersecurity. Enterprises are advised to prioritize protection against 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks, where sensitive data is intercepted today for future decryption by quantum-capable adversaries. The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is framed as a manageable, phased evolution rather than an immediate crisis, allowing firms to modernize infrastructure without systemic disruption.

items.text: Global sovereign bond yields have reached levels not seen since July 2008, with US 30-year Treasury auctions recently clearing at 5.216%, the highest rate since 2001. The rise in real yields to 2.41% on the 10-year Treasury creates a significant hurdle for non-yielding assets like Bitcoin, as investors can now achieve inflation-adjusted returns with minimal risk.

items.title: Bond Yields Pressure Markets as AI Stocks Rally and Fed Rate Hike Bets Fade
items.text: Market participants are navigating a complex environment where rising bond yields exert downward pressure on valuations while simultaneous rallies in AI-related equities suggest persistent risk-on sentiment. The fading expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes indicate that the market is pricing in a plateau in the tightening cycle, shifting focus toward the duration of current high-interest rate regimes.

items.title: The end of an era for China's economy - Noahpinion
items.text: The passing of former Premier Zhu Rongji marks the symbolic conclusion of the high-growth era defined by WTO accession, aggressive privatization of state-owned enterprises, and significant tax reforms. Current economic growth has decelerated to an official 5%, with independent analysts suggesting actual performance may be as low as 2-3%, signaling a fundamental shift away from the previous export-led model.

items.title: To rent or not to rent? That is the question for Hong Kong homebuyers
items.text: The Centa-City Rental Index has surged 5.2% year-to-date through July 2026, reflecting a tightening residential market that is forcing potential tenants to reconsider the cost-benefit analysis of homeownership. Rising rental costs are incentivizing some buyers to enter the market, as mortgage payments on entry-level properties can now be lower than monthly rental outlays, provided the buyer can meet substantial down payment requirements.

items.title: Hong Kong banks eye higher interest income despite property drag
items.text: Major local lenders like BOCHK are projecting growth in pre-provisioning operating profit, supported by resilient net interest income and a 6.2% year-on-year increase in total system-wide loans as of June 2026. Despite broader growth, banks remain burdened by exposure to small local property developers, necessitating ongoing de-risking processes that continue to weigh on the earnings performance of institutions like the Bank of East Asia.

items.title: The AI boom is reviving America’s nuclear dream
items.text: Major tech firms including Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta are shifting energy strategies toward nuclear power to secure the 24/7 reliable electricity required for high-density AI data centers. The intermittency of wind and solar, combined with the high cost of long-duration battery storage, has forced these companies to pivot from purely renewable goals to nuclear investments to maintain their net-zero pledges.

items.title: Big Tech’s data centre boom poised to drive up carbon emissions
items.text: The rapid expansion of AI-focused data centers is creating a surge in electricity demand that is currently outpacing the capacity of local grids to provide carbon-free energy. Investors should monitor potential regulatory risks and ESG-related valuation impacts as tech companies struggle to reconcile massive infrastructure growth with their long-term corporate carbon-neutrality commitments.

items.title: Google reportedly taps AMD to design next-generation TPU — hybrid AI ASIC could integrate on-package CPU cores for reinforcement learning
items.text: Google is reportedly collaborating with AMD on its 10th-generation TPU, marking a significant shift toward integrating general-purpose CPU cores directly into custom AI ASICs to handle reinforcement learning workloads. The move suggests that Google is prioritizing agentic AI and reasoning capabilities, which require higher CPU-to-accelerator ratios than traditional large language model training, potentially impacting future data center hardware architectures.

items.title: Alibaba Overtakes Google and Meta With 3 Billion AI Model Downloads
items.text: Alibaba’s Qwen model family has achieved over 3 billion downloads in six months, significantly outpacing Google and Meta and establishing itself as a dominant force in the global open-source AI ecosystem. The high adoption rate among developers indicates that Alibaba’s open-source strategy is successfully gaining traction outside of China, challenging the market influence of American tech giants in the enterprise software and fine-tuning space.

items.title: NVIDIA’s $3 Billion Bet on the Power Behind AI
items.text: Nvidia is investing up to $3 billion in Lancium, a power infrastructure developer, to secure critical grid interconnections for AI data centers like the Stargate project. This move signals a strategic shift where Nvidia is directly financing the physical infrastructure layer—land and power—to mitigate the electricity bottlenecks currently limiting its GPU deployment scale.

items.title: Nvidia AI Financing Is The $500 Billion Risk Investors Aren’t Watching
items.text: Major financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs and BlackRock, are mobilizing $500 billion to finance AI infrastructure, with Nvidia acting as a central marketplace for these 'compute bonds.' Critics, including Michael Burry, warn that this complex web of private credit and off-balance-sheet commitments creates significant leverage risks that could mirror pre-2008 financial instability.

items.title: This Week in Tesla: Elon Musk's Financial Windfall, EV Sales Fall and More
items.text: North American EV sales experienced a significant contraction, falling 27% in July to 140,000 units, contributing to an 18% year-to-date decline compared to the same period in 2025. Tesla's corporate governance and valuation are under scrutiny following reports of a $158 billion 2025 pay package for Elon Musk, alongside potential performance-based windfalls tied to a possible merger with SpaceX.

items.title: EVs Slashed Global Fuel Consumption Massively In 2025
items.text: Global plug-in vehicle adoption displaced 2.3 million barrels of oil per day in 2025, with projections indicating this figure could reach 5.3 million barrels daily by 2030. While passenger cars are expected to drive future displacement, electric two- and three-wheelers currently account for a larger share of daily oil reduction, totaling 1.1 million barrels per day.

items.title: SpaceX is Planning to Spend Up to $500 Billion on Data Centers. Here's Why Elon Musk is Pushing All-In
items.text: SpaceX is aggressively scaling its AI compute capacity from 1.4 gigawatts to a target of 6 to 10 gigawatts, with projected capital expenditures reaching $300 billion to $500 billion by 2027. The company is leveraging high-margin inference economics, securing multi-billion dollar rental agreements with Anthropic and Google that demonstrate significant revenue potential per gigawatt of compute capacity.

items.title: Temple data centers respond to Gov. Abbott’s new standards to protect local communities
items.text: Texas has implemented strict new utility and transparency standards requiring data center developers to disclose projected electricity and water usage, effectively ending the practice of shifting infrastructure costs to residential ratepayers. Major tech firms including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have signed the federal Ratepayer Protection Pledge, signaling a broader regulatory shift that forces developers to internalize the true cost of grid and resource consumption.

items.title: SpaceX Establishes 38-Minute Dual-Coast Launch Record as Industry Evaluates High-Cadence Benchmarks
items.text: SpaceX achieved a record-breaking 38.5-minute turnaround between orbital launches on opposite coasts, demonstrating an operational model that treats launch pads like high-efficiency airport gates. This high-cadence capability, now exceeding 160 missions annually, serves as a significant competitive barrier to entry by maximizing infrastructure utilization and maintaining cost leadership in the launch market.

items.title: Rocket Lab Announces Successful Launch of Eight Satellite Platforms for MDA Space and Globalstar
items.text: Rocket Lab successfully deployed eight 500kg satellites for MDA Space, marking the start of a 17-platform contract valued at $143 million to support Globalstar's direct-to-device communications. The mission validates Rocket Lab's 'Lightning' satellite platform, which is currently in production for additional U.S. government and defense constellations, signaling a shift toward higher-value space systems manufacturing.

items.title: Chery-JLR's Freelander 8 tops 10,000 pre-orders in first 48 hours
items.text: The Freelander 8, a luxury extended-range SUV from the Chery-JLR joint venture, secured over 10,000 pre-orders within 48 hours of its August 14 launch. Pricing for the five variants ranges from 339,900 yuan ($50,080) to 459,900 yuan, targeting the premium segment with high-performance specs including 610 kW of power. The vehicle features advanced technology integration, including Huawei's Qiankun ADS 5 and the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8397 chip, which provides 320 TOPS of computing power. Built on an 800-volt 6C platform, the SUV utilizes a 60.3 kWh CATL battery capable of charging from 20% to 80% in 12 minutes.

items.title: GAC Aion to debut Ray 7, first model in Ray lineup, on August 19
items.text: GAC Aion will debut the Ray 7 on August 19, a mid-to-large-size electric sedan designed to capture the younger demographic and spearhead a new product lineup. The vehicle is powered by a 180-kW Huawei-supplied motor and utilizes LFP batteries sourced from both CATL and GAC Aion's subsidiary, Yinpai Battery. The Ray 7 introduces GAC Aion's new brand logo and features a 'Super Chassis' with chip-level drive-control integration, alongside an optional LiDAR-based driver-assistance system. This launch follows a strong recovery for GAC Aion, which reported a 62.08% year-on-year sales increase for the first seven months of 2026.

items.title: From Tokens To Tasks: Why Agentic AI Changes The Infrastructure Conversation
items.text: The shift from prompt-based AI to agentic AI requires infrastructure to support complex, multi-step workflows rather than simple token generation. Agentic AI demands higher reliability and tighter integration between compute, memory, and networking to handle autonomous decision-making cycles. Infrastructure providers must now optimize for the entire task lifecycle, including the orchestration of fragmented tool ecosystems and continuous verification.

items.title: Japan’s 10-year bond yield hits 3-decade high as inflation, central bank pressures mount
items.text: The benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield reached 2.925%, a level not seen since September 1996, as global debt markets face a broad bearish trend. Economic data revealed Japan's annualized growth slowed to 1.1% in the April-June quarter, significantly missing the 2% median forecast due to flat consumption and a 1.2% decline in capital spending.

items.title: European Central Bank blog post forecasts an AI market correction
items.text: An ECB blog post warns that current tech stock valuations are detached from fundamentals, noting that even if AI profit growth materializes, it may struggle to meet the market's excessively optimistic expectations. European financial stability is at risk from a potential U.S. correction, as households and institutions hold approximately 440 billion euros in exposure to the 'Magnificent Seven' tech stocks.

items.title: Ditch inflation targets? Better to overhaul them instead
items.text: Central banks face increasing difficulty maintaining 2% inflation targets due to structural disruptions from AI, global supply chain shifts, and geopolitical shocks that render traditional models less effective. Monetary authorities are urged to move beyond simple target setting by providing clearer communication on alternative economic scenarios to prevent policy from becoming untethered in an unpredictable landscape.

items.title: Berkshire's Alphabet stake, Meta goes back to court, Europe's champagne problems and more in Morning Squawk
items.text: Berkshire Hathaway disclosed a $17 billion investment in Alphabet during the second quarter, establishing the Google parent as the conglomerate's third-largest equity holding. Nvidia revealed its stake in SpaceX is valued at approximately $21 billion, while legal pressures mount for Meta as it faces a multi-state lawsuit led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta.

items.title: 'Don't get too comfortable': Wall Street’s ‘fear gauge’ hits 2026 low — here's why it's unlikely to last
items.text: The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) reached a 2026 low of 14.2, signaling significant investor complacency despite historical data indicating mid-August to mid-October is a period of heightened downside risk. Market technicians warn that the S&P 500's 16% year-to-date gain, combined with the lack of significant downside volume days, suggests a potential correction is overdue as markets enter a historically volatile calendar window.

items.title: AI is driving up Treasury yields: ‘It just touches everything’
items.text: Investment-grade corporate bond issuance has surged to nearly $1.5 trillion this year, a 36% increase that is straining the market's capacity to absorb debt alongside record US government deficits. Tech giants are driving a massive borrowing spree, with Nvidia alone reportedly seeking $500 billion for AI infrastructure, effectively competing with the Treasury for capital and forcing yields higher across the curve.

items.title: Global Market: Euro zone bond yields hover near 15-year highs as Middle East war fuels inflation fears
items.text: German 10-year Bund yields are testing 15-year highs near 3.21%, as markets price in a 90% probability of an ECB rate hike in September to combat energy-driven inflation. The yield spread between Italian and German bonds has widened to 77 basis points, signaling increased investor risk aversion toward peripheral euro zone debt amid geopolitical instability in the Middle East.

items.title: Anchored by resilience, new growth drivers reshape China's growth
items.text: China reported a 4.7% year-on-year GDP growth for the first half of 2026, reaching 69.57 trillion yuan, as the economy pivots from property-led expansion toward high-tech and green manufacturing. While service consumption remains buoyant, structural divergence persists with weak demand for durable goods and real estate investment, forcing a reliance on export-oriented sectors to maintain growth momentum.

items.title: China House Price Index Shows Slower Decline in July, Improving to -3.2%
items.text: The China House Price Index recorded a marginal improvement to -3.2% in July from -3.3% in June, marking two consecutive months of slight recovery following government-led stimulus efforts. Despite the stabilization, the sector remains in deep contraction, with developer defaults and high unsold inventory continuing to weigh heavily on consumer confidence and overall domestic demand.

items.title: URA swings to $338m surplus after three years of losses
items.text: The Urban Renewal Authority (URA) returned to a $338 million operating surplus in the 2025/26 fiscal year, marking a significant turnaround after three consecutive years of net losses totaling billions. The government is currently reviewing the URA's financial and operational models, including acquisition policies, to ensure long-term sustainability amid ongoing volatility in the local property market.

items.title: Northern Metropolis: Hong Kong homebuyers flock to flats launch
items.text: Wheelock Properties successfully sold over half of the 82 units at its Park Silicon project, providing a critical sentiment boost following a 42 percent decline in total home sales during July. The strong reception in the Northern Metropolis suggests that property prices may be stabilizing after recent lows, though developers remain cautious as buyers evaluate higher asking prices.

items.title: Big Tech companies have $3T in hidden AI expenditures- report
items.text: Analysts have identified approximately $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet or obscured AI-related expenditures across major technology firms, suggesting the true cost of the current infrastructure buildout is significantly higher than reported. This massive capital commitment, largely directed toward data center expansion and AI hardware, raises concerns about the long-term return on investment and the sustainability of current spending levels for companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft.

items.title: Tech companies’ AI debt surges as Oracle nears junk credit rating
items.text: Oracle's fiscal 2026 capital expenditure reached $55.66 billion, exceeding its own guidance, with projections for 2027 reaching $95 billion as the company shifts toward debt-funded growth strategies. S&P Global has downgraded Oracle to BBB-, one notch above junk status, while credit spreads for other major tech firms like Meta and Amazon are widening as markets demand higher risk premiums for AI-driven debt.

items.title: Nvidia backing $105 billion in financing for OpenAI data center in Ohio
items.text: Nvidia is providing a $105 billion financing guarantee for a massive data center project in Ohio, which will support an initial 4.25 gigawatts of computing capacity with potential for expansion to 8 gigawatts. The deal includes a $1.5 billion direct investment from Nvidia into SB Energy, highlighting a strategic shift where the chipmaker is actively financing the infrastructure required to sustain demand for its high-end AI compute products.

items.title: Higgsfield's valuation soars fourfold to $5.4 billion in six months on AI content demand
items.text: Higgsfield has achieved a $5.4 billion valuation, representing a 400% increase in just six months, driven by explosive market demand for AI-generated content tools. The rapid valuation surge underscores the intense investor appetite for specialized AI software applications that can scale content production, signaling a potential shift in capital allocation toward high-growth generative AI startups.

items.title: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
items.text: Nvidia is anchoring a massive $105 billion infrastructure project in Ohio, signaling a strategic shift toward financing the physical data center capacity required to sustain its high-end GPU demand. CEO Jensen Huang projects this specific facility could eventually generate $600 billion in revenue, highlighting the company's aggressive efforts to secure long-term compute utilization through direct capital commitments.

items.title: Nvidia financing initiative follows SEC guidance that takes sponsors off the hook for data center investments
items.text: Recent SEC guidance exempting certain data center debt from Dodd-Frank risk retention rules is enabling Nvidia to orchestrate $500 billion in partially backstopped agreements with private equity firms. This regulatory tailwind allows sponsors to reduce required equity in deals, effectively creating a new, highly leveraged asset class for computing power that accelerates the build-out of AI infrastructure.

items.title: UK Opens ZEV Mandate Review as Softer EV Sales Targets Come Onto the Table
items.text: The UK government has launched a formal consultation to review the ZEV Mandate, which currently requires 80% of new car sales to be zero-emission by 2030 and 100% by 2035. Industry leaders and the SMMT argue that current targets are unsustainable, forcing manufacturers to spend billions on artificial incentives to stimulate demand that does not match the mandated supply trajectory.

items.title: Europe’s subsidy-driven growth lifts global EV sales 9% in July
items.text: Global EV sales reached 1.85 million units in July 2026, a 9% year-on-year increase, with Europe serving as the primary growth engine due to aggressive subsidy programs in France, Germany, and the UK. Regional divergence remains significant, as North American sales contracted by 27% year-on-year, highlighting the sensitivity of global EV adoption to federal incentive structures and policy comparisons.

items.title: Nvidia to invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy under OpenAI data center deal
items.text: Nvidia is providing a $105 billion guarantee to support OpenAI's 20-year lease of an 8-gigawatt data center in Ohio, marking a significant expansion of the chipmaker's infrastructure financing strategy. The deal includes a $1.5 billion direct investment in SB Energy and establishes Nvidia as the exclusive chip provider, effectively securing long-term demand for its compute hardware through deep integration with customer infrastructure.

items.title: PJM’s New Deal for Data Centers: Bring Power or Face Cuts
items.text: PJM Interconnection has proposed a new reliability framework that would allow large data centers to connect to the grid before sufficient capacity is available, provided they accept the risk of earlier emergency curtailment. Facilities with a peak demand of 50 MW or more can mitigate this risk through 'Bring Your Own New Capacity' (BYONC) programs, forcing developers to internalize the cost of grid stability to avoid operational disruptions.

items.title: Satellite operators emphasize launch deals in a constrained market
items.text: Satellite operators are increasingly securing launch capacity years in advance to mitigate risks from a constrained market, as evidenced by AST SpaceMobile's reliance on a multi-provider strategy to complete its 45-satellite constellation. The grounding of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket has forced operators to pivot back to SpaceX's Falcon 9, creating potential deployment bottlenecks due to the Falcon 9's lower per-launch satellite capacity compared to the larger New Glenn vehicle.

items.title: Space ETF race heats up with two new European launches
items.text: The rapid introduction of space-themed ETFs by Global X, First Trust, BlackRock, and WisdomTree in Europe signals growing institutional interest in space as a distinct, investable asset class despite the current small AUM of these funds. These products utilize strict revenue-threshold filters—requiring 40-50% of revenue from space-related activities—to ensure investors gain pure-play exposure rather than dilution from diversified defense or industrial conglomerates.

items.title: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
items.text: Stripe's reported acquisition of OpenRouter signals a strategic pivot toward becoming a central aggregator in the fragmented AI model market. By controlling the infrastructure layer for AI model access, Stripe aims to capture value from the increasing commoditization of LLMs. This move represents a fundamental shift in Stripe's business model, moving beyond pure payment processing to owning the underlying utility layer for AI-driven applications. The acquisition positions Stripe to benefit from the 'Aggregation Theory' by reducing friction for developers to switch between various AI providers, thereby cementing Stripe's role as the essential platform for the digital economy.

items.title: 800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid To Gate
items.text: AI data center power requirements are shifting from 125kW to 500kW and eventually 1MW, necessitating a transition to 800VDC architectures to manage efficiency. The industry is moving away from traditional multi-stage power conversion toward streamlined architectures that reduce energy loss between the medium-voltage grid and sub-1V GPU rails. Hyperscalers are increasingly adopting solid-state transformers to minimize conversion stages, which is forcing component suppliers to fundamentally rethink power electronics design. Thermal management and power density have become primary bottlenecks, as the efficiency of the entire conversion path directly impacts the performance and reliability of AI accelerators.

items.title: Geely Auto lifts export goal to 920,000 as overseas becomes only growth engine
items.text: Geely Auto has aggressively raised its 2026 export target to 920,000 vehicles, a 44% increase from its original guidance and nearly double the 2025 export volume. Overseas markets have become the company's primary growth engine, as domestic sales in China declined 22.6% during the first half of the year. New energy vehicles (NEVs) are driving this international expansion, accounting for 59% of total exports in July with a 616% year-on-year growth rate.

items.title: CATL says core operations carbon neutral by end-2025, supply chain next
items.text: CATL has achieved carbon neutrality across its core operations by the end of 2025, utilizing 100% zero-carbon electricity across its manufacturing bases. The company has set a new goal to achieve value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035, a significant challenge given that over 80% of product emissions originate from the supply chain. To manage this transition, CATL has implemented a full-chain carbon data traceability platform to monitor emissions from mineral extraction through component manufacturing.

items.title: The Download: dead robot friends and the “censorship-industrial complex”
items.text: The US government is actively pressuring international allies to reject China’s rival AI initiatives, signaling a shift toward a bifurcated global AI landscape. The 'censorship-industrial complex' theory, which alleges coordinated suppression of conservative speech by government and tech entities, has transitioned from fringe discourse into official US policy. items.title: Rupee weakens, bond yields rise as RBI shuts FCNR(B) swap window early
items.text: The Reserve Bank of India's decision to close its concessional FCNR(B) swap facility early has triggered market volatility, pushing the 10-year government bond yield to 6.81%. Investors are concerned that the premature termination of this liquidity window will constrain dollar inflows, exacerbating pressure on the rupee amid persistent demand from oil importers.

items.title: China's Economy Is Not Collapsing. It Is Being Rolled Over.
items.text: Official data reveals a stark divergence in the economy, with high-tech manufacturing and exports growing by 13.3% and 13.4% respectively, while real-estate investment continues to contract sharply at -18.0%. The Chinese government is effectively managing a 'rollover' of bad debt through state-controlled banks, which prevents a systemic financial collapse but leaves the economy burdened by assets that fail to generate adequate returns.

items.title: People: Hongkong Land's Neil Anderson Departs After 2 Decades
items.text: The departure of Neil Anderson, a key figure in the Central portfolio, underscores the significant strategic pivot of Hongkong Land as it transitions from a traditional developer model to a fund management structure. This leadership change follows the company's March rollout of a new portfolio-CEO structure, signaling a long-term shift in how the firm manages its prime commercial assets and capital allocation strategies.

items.title: Layoff fears are pushing some visa holders out of Big Tech
items.text: Repeated layoffs across the 'Magnificent 7,' which have totaled over 100,000 jobs since 2022, are prompting high-skilled visa holders to abandon Big Tech for more stable, specialized sectors like semiconductor equipment manufacturing. items.text: Nvidia is providing a $105 billion lease guarantee to support an OpenAI data center in Ohio, marking a massive expansion of the chipmaker's role as an infrastructure financier. items.text: Trane Technologies and Eaton have launched a medium-voltage reference design that claims to improve energy efficiency by 15% while reducing copper usage by 80% in AI data centers. items.title: Blue Origin adding second pad to Cape Canaveral launch complex amid rocket explosion repairs
items.text: Blue Origin is expanding its Cape Canaveral facility to a dual-pad configuration, aiming to support the larger New Glenn 9x4 rocket alongside the existing 7x2 variant currently undergoing post-explosion repairs.
